entries.title: は
entries.summary_en: Marks a topic or contrast.
entries.explanation_en: は sets a noun or phrase as the topic that the following statement addresses. It can also contrast that topic with alternatives. As a particle, it is pronounced わ, though written は. It does not by itself mark the grammatical subject; が often marks the subject within the statement about the topic.

formation.explanation_en: Attach は to the phrase being presented as the topic or contrast.

entries.title: です
entries.summary_en: Polite nonpast copula used to identify or describe something.
entries.explanation_en: です gives a statement a polite tone and links a topic or subject with a noun or adjective predicate. With a noun predicate, it corresponds broadly to “is” or “am”; it does not change for person or number.

formation.explanation_en: Place です after a noun predicate to make a polite nonpast statement.

notes_en: です is a copula, not a lexical verb meaning “exist.”

entries.title: ます-form negative (ません)
entries.summary_en: Forms a polite negative verb statement.
entries.explanation_en: Add ません to a verb's ます-stem to make a polite negative statement. For example, 分かる becomes 分かりません; ある and いる follow the same pattern, giving ありません and いません.

formation.explanation_en: Add ません to the ます-stem.

entries.title: で (place of action or event)
entries.summary_en: Marks the place or setting where an action or event takes place.
entries.explanation_en: で locates an action or event in the place named before it. Use it for activities and events that occur at a location. For the location where something exists or resides, に is generally used instead.

formation.explanation_en: Attach で to the place where an action or event occurs.

notes_en: Contrast event location で with existence or residence location に.

entries.title: 動詞のた形
entries.summary_en: Marks a verb as past or completed in plain style.
entries.explanation_en: The plain past form presents an event or action as past or completed. Its formation depends on the verb class.

formation.form: Ichidan verb: remove final る + た
formation.explanation_en: Remove final る and add た, as in 見る → 見た.
Change the final kana according to the verb’s past-form pattern; the resulting form ends in た or だ.

formation.form: する → した; 来る → 来た（きた）
formation.explanation_en: Use these irregular plain past forms.

entries.title: 疑問詞・節 + か
entries.reading: ぎもんし・せつ + か
entries.summary_en: Makes a question word or question-shaped clause an embedded unknown.
entries.explanation_en: Place か after a question word or a question-shaped clause to mark it as an unknown within a larger statement. The embedded clause keeps its own predicate form; the larger sentence supplies the surrounding assertion or question. This use of か does not create a standalone question.

formation.explanation_en: Put か after the clause containing the unknown, then follow it with a predicate such as 分かる or 知る.
A plain-form predicate can precede か when the whole proposition is the embedded unknown.

notes_en: Embedded か differs from sentence-final か, which can mark a direct question.

entries.title: い形容詞の連体形
entries.reading: いけいようしのれんたいけい
entries.summary_en: An i-adjective directly modifies a following noun in its nonpast form.
entries.explanation_en: An i-adjective in its plain nonpast form can immediately precede a noun and describe it. It retains its final い in this attributive use.

formation.explanation_en: Place the nonpast i-adjective directly before the noun it modifies, as in 暗い所.

entries.title: の (noun modifier)
entries.summary_en: Links nouns to express relations such as possession, association, location, or category.
entries.explanation_en: の connects a modifying noun to the noun that follows. The relationship is inferred from the nouns and context: it can express possession, association, or a spatial relation such as the relation between a place and its interior. The modifier comes before の and the head noun follows it.

formation.explanation_en: Use Noun 1 to qualify or relate to Noun 2.

notes_en: Do not assume every の phrase expresses literal ownership.

entries.title: ている
entries.summary_en: Expresses an ongoing action or a continuing state resulting from an event.
entries.explanation_en: Attach いる to a verb's て-form. With an activity verb, ている commonly describes an action in progress; with a change-of-state verb, it can describe the resulting state. The interpretation depends on the verb and context.

formation.explanation_en: Attach いる to the て-form to express an ongoing action or resulting state.

entries.title: を (direct object)
entries.summary_en: Marks the direct object of a transitive verb.
entries.explanation_en: を marks the participant or thing directly acted on by a transitive verb. It follows the object noun phrase.

formation.explanation_en: Attach を to the direct object before the verb.

notes_en: The particle を is pronounced お.

entries.title: ます形の過去 (ました)
entries.summary_en: Forms the polite past of a verb.
entries.explanation_en: Add ました to a verb's ます-stem to present an action or event as past in polite speech. The verb supplies the lexical meaning; ました marks polite past inflection.

formation.explanation_en: Add ました to the ます-stem.

entries.title: が (subject marker)
entries.summary_en: Marks the subject associated with the predicate.
entries.explanation_en: が marks the noun phrase identified as the subject of a predicate. It often introduces new or focused information.

formation.explanation_en: Attach が to the subject noun before its predicate.

notes_en: Contrast が, which marks a clause subject, with は, which marks a topic or contrast.

entries.title: でした
entries.summary_en: Polite past form of the copula です.
entries.explanation_en: でした is the polite past copula, used after a noun or adjectival noun predicate to present a past identification or description. It is distinct from the polite past ending ました used with verbs.

formation.explanation_en: Place でした after a noun predicate to make a polite past statement.

notes_en: No candidate in this set uses でした; the polite past verb entry is ました.

entries.title: へ (direction or destination)
entries.summary_en: Marks the direction or destination toward which movement is directed; pronounced e as a particle.
entries.explanation_en: へ follows a place or destination and presents it as the direction of movement. It emphasizes orientation toward a destination. に can also mark destinations, while を can mark a route traversed.

formation.explanation_en: Attach へ to the place toward which movement is directed.

notes_en: The particle is written へ and pronounced え.
Movement verbs can also take に for a destination, with overlapping uses.

entries.title: 受身形
entries.summary_en: Forms a passive verb, presenting an affected participant as the subject.
entries.explanation_en: The passive presents an affected participant as the subject. With a transitive verb, its object can become the passive subject, and the agent may be marked with に. Japanese also uses passive forms for events that affect a person. The agent can be omitted when it is unknown or unimportant.

formation.form: Ichidan verb: remove final る + られる
formation.explanation_en: Remove final る and add られる, as in 捨てる → 捨てられる.

formation.form: Godan verb: final u-row kana changes to the corresponding a-row kana + れる
formation.explanation_en: Change the final kana to the corresponding a-row kana and add れる; verbs ending in う use わ before れる.

formation.form: する → される; 来る → 来られる（こられる）
formation.explanation_en: Use these irregular passive forms.

entries.title: も (addition in a negative clause)
entries.summary_en: Adds another item to a negative statement, often conveying “also not” or “neither.”
entries.explanation_en: も can replace a particle such as が or を to add a noun phrase to the statement. In a negative clause, it commonly means that the added item is also absent or also does not participate in the action.

formation.explanation_en: Use も after an added noun phrase when the negative predicate applies to it as well.

notes_en: The interpretation depends on the polarity and scope of the predicate.

entries.title: に (position or orientation with 見る)
entries.summary_en: Marks a position or orientation in which something is seen.
entries.explanation_en: に can mark the position or orientation associated with seeing something. In patterns such as Nを位置に見る, を marks the thing seen and に marks its relative position from the viewer's perspective.

formation.form: Thing + を + position + に + 見る
formation.explanation_en: Mark the viewed thing with を and its position or orientation with に.

notes_en: This positional に differs from the destination or resulting-position に used with verbs such as 置く.

entries.title: Vます-stem + ながら
entries.summary_en: Shows that one action takes place while another action is performed.
entries.explanation_en: Attach ながら to a verb's ます-stem to show that this action occurs while the main predicate's action takes place. The ながら action and main predicate normally have the same understood subject. The main predicate usually follows and carries the sentence's tense and politeness.

formation.explanation_en: Attach ながら to the ます-stem.

entries.title: 連用形（ます語幹）
entries.reading: れんようけい（ますごかん）
entries.summary_en: The verb stem used before ます and in compact links between predicates.
entries.explanation_en: In ordinary verb conjugation, 連用形 is the stem before ます, also called the ます-stem: 歩き is the stem in 歩きます. A bare 連用形 can link an action to a following predicate, especially in written or compact sequences.

formation.form: Godan verb: final u-row kana → corresponding i-row kana
formation.explanation_en: Change the final kana to the corresponding i-row kana, as in 歩く → 歩き.
Remove final る, as in 見る → 見.

formation.form: する → し; 来る → き
formation.explanation_en: Use these irregular ます-stems.

entries.title: に (resulting position)
entries.summary_en: Marks the resulting location or position where something is placed or assigned.
entries.explanation_en: に marks the resulting location or position associated with verbs such as 置く. It identifies where an object is placed or what position it is assigned. This differs from で, which can mark the location where an action takes place.

formation.form: Resulting place or position + に + verb
formation.explanation_en: Attach に to the resulting location or position before the verb.

notes_en: With 置く, に marks where the object is placed; the placed object is commonly marked with を.

entries.title: 動詞のて形 (接続)
entries.summary_en: Connects a verb to following material or links actions and clauses.
entries.explanation_en: The て-form connects a verb to following material. It can link successive actions or clauses; the precise relationship depends on the context and what follows.

formation.form: Ichidan verb: remove final る + て
formation.explanation_en: Remove final る and add て, as in 見る → 見て.

formation.form: Godan verb: て-form sound change + て or で
formation.explanation_en: Change the final kana according to the verb’s て-form pattern; some forms end in て and others in で.

formation.form: する → して; 来る → 来て（きて）
formation.explanation_en: Use these irregular て-forms.

entries.title: Vてやる
entries.summary_en: Expresses doing an action for someone, with a casual tone that can sound blunt or condescending.
entries.explanation_en: Attach やる to a verb's て-form to describe doing that action for someone. It can express a favor or benevolent act, but やる is casual and may sound blunt or condescending when directed toward a person. The main verb retains its lexical meaning.

formation.explanation_en: Attach やる to the て-form to present the action as done for someone.

entries.title: 動詞の命令形
entries.reading: どうしのめいれいけい
entries.summary_en: Directly commands or urges someone to perform an action.
entries.explanation_en: The imperative is a direct command form of a verb. Its tone is often forceful or blunt, so the appropriate choice depends on the relationship and situation.

formation.form: Godan verb: final u-row kana → corresponding e-row kana
formation.explanation_en: Change the final kana to the corresponding e-row kana, as in 書く → 書け.

formation.form: Ichidan verb: remove final る and add ろ or よ
formation.explanation_en: ろ is common in direct speech; よ is a less common, often formal or literary alternative.

formation.form: する → しろ; 来る → 来い（こい）
formation.explanation_en: Use these irregular imperative forms.

entries.title: と (quotation)
entries.summary_en: Marks quoted words or thought before a verb of saying or thinking.
entries.explanation_en: と closes quoted content and links it to a verb such as 言う or 思う. The quoted material can be a sentence or a short expression.

formation.form: Quoted content + と + saying or thinking verb
formation.explanation_en: Place と after the quoted words and before the verb that reports them.

notes_en: Direct quotation commonly preserves the speaker’s original wording.

entries.title: に (location of residence)
entries.summary_en: Marks the place where someone or something lives or resides.
entries.explanation_en: に marks the location associated with a state of residence, commonly with verbs such as 住む. It identifies where the subject lives, rather than where an action takes place. Use で for an event or activity occurring at a location.

formation.explanation_en: Attach に to the place where the subject resides.

notes_en: Contrast residence location に with event location で.

entries.title: Vることにする
entries.summary_en: Expresses a decision to do the action described by the preceding verb.
entries.explanation_en: Put a plain nonpast verb before ことにする to present that action as a decision or resolution by the subject. ことにする presents a choice made by the subject, while ことになる presents an outcome settled by circumstances or others.

formation.form: Verb plain nonpast + ことにする
formation.explanation_en: Attach ことにする to a plain nonpast verb to state a decision.

entries.title: が (clause contrast)
entries.summary_en: Connects clauses with a contrast or qualification, often comparable to “but.”
entries.explanation_en: Clause-linking が follows a clause and introduces a related clause that contrasts with or qualifies it. It does not mark a subject in this use. The precise force can range from a mild contrast to a concession, depending on context.

formation.explanation_en: Place が after the first clause to connect it to a contrasting or qualifying clause.

notes_en: Distinguish clause-linking が from subject-marking が.

entries.title: ます形 (polite nonpast)
entries.summary_en: Forms a polite nonpast verb statement.
entries.explanation_en: Add ます to a verb's ます-stem to form a polite nonpast statement. Depending on context, it can describe a habit, general fact, or future event.

formation.explanation_en: Add ます to the ます-stem.

entries.title: である
entries.summary_en: A formal plain copula that identifies or describes something.
entries.explanation_en: である connects a noun or な-adjective to a predicate, similar in meaning to plain だ but more formal and often used in writing. Its connective form で links the identification or description to following material.

formation.form: Noun / な-adjective stem + である
formation.explanation_en: Add である after a noun or な-adjective stem to make a formal plain assertion.
The connective form links the preceding identification or description to what follows.

entries.title: 動詞のない形
entries.summary_en: Forms the plain negative of a verb.
entries.explanation_en: The plain negative says that an action does not happen or is not done. It is also used before other expressions that require a negative verb form.

formation.explanation_en: Remove final る and add ない.

formation.form: Godan: final う-row kana → corresponding あ-row kana + ない
formation.explanation_en: For verbs ending in う, change う to わ before ない.

formation.form: する → しない; 来る（くる）→ 来ない（こない）
formation.explanation_en: These common verbs have irregular negative forms.

entries.title: い形容詞のて形
entries.reading: いけいようしのてけい
entries.summary_en: Connects an i-adjective to following material or another description.
entries.explanation_en: The connective form links descriptions, gives a reason or circumstance, or connects an adjective to further material. Its interpretation depends on the surrounding clause.

formation.form: い-adjective: replace final い with くて
formation.explanation_en: For example, 暗い becomes 暗くて.

entries.title: 動詞・節 + こと
entries.reading: どうし・せつ + こと
entries.summary_en: Turns an action or clause into an abstract fact, event, or matter.
entries.explanation_en: こと follows a plain-form clause and lets the clause function as a noun phrase. It can refer to an action, event, or fact as a whole.

formation.explanation_en: Place こと after a clause in plain form to nominalize it.

entries.title: だけ
entries.summary_en: Limits a phrase to the stated amount or scope.
entries.explanation_en: だけ follows the phrase it limits and means ‘only’ or ‘just’. It can attach to nouns, quantities, and clauses; は after だけ can add topic or contrast emphasis.

formation.explanation_en: Place だけ after the item or clause whose scope is restricted.

entries.title: 動詞辞書形 + と
entries.reading: どうしじしょけい + と
entries.summary_en: Marks a condition that regularly, naturally, or immediately leads to a result.
entries.explanation_en: と joins a condition to its consequence, often describing a predictable result, a repeated outcome, or what happens upon an action. The result clause generally does not express a command or the speaker’s intention.

formation.explanation_en: Attach と to the dictionary form of the verb that states the condition.

entries.title: 動詞 plain form + こともある
entries.reading: どうし plain form + こともある
entries.summary_en: Says that an action or event sometimes occurs.
entries.explanation_en: This pattern presents the nominalized action as one possibility among others. It describes occasional occurrence, rather than a single event that is happening now.

formation.explanation_en: Nominalize the action with こと.
もある presents the event as one possibility or occurrence among others.

entries.title: 伝聞のそうだ
entries.summary_en: Reports information heard from another source.
entries.explanation_en: Attached to a plain-form predicate, そうだ presents the preceding information as something reported or heard. It does not mean that something merely looks likely; that appearance reading uses a different attachment pattern.

formation.explanation_en: Attach そうだ to the plain form of a verb, adjective, or copula predicate.

entries.title: Vないで
entries.summary_en: Describes doing something without performing the preceding action.
entries.explanation_en: ないで follows a negative verb form to describe an action or state carried out in the absence of that verb’s action. It can also occur in requests meaning ‘please don’t’; the surrounding context distinguishes the uses.

formation.explanation_en: Form the plain negative and add で.
The negative verb form supplies the action that is omitted.

entries.title: い形容詞のない形
entries.reading: いけいようしのないけい
entries.summary_en: Forms the plain negative of an i-adjective.
entries.explanation_en: The plain negative says that the quality described by an i-adjective is absent. This form can also modify nouns or connect to further predicates.

formation.form: Replace final い with くない
formation.explanation_en: For example, 怖い becomes 怖くない.

entries.title: い形容詞の過去否定
entries.reading: いけいようしのかこひてい
entries.summary_en: Says that an i-adjective quality was absent in the past.
entries.explanation_en: The past negative combines the adjective’s negative form with the past form of ない.

formation.form: Replace final い with くない
formation.explanation_en: First form the plain negative of the i-adjective.

formation.form: Replace final い in ない with かった
formation.explanation_en: The negative ending becomes なかった, as in 怖くなかった.

entries.title: N + のようだ
entries.summary_en: Compares something to a noun or describes it as seeming similar to one.
entries.explanation_en: のようだ presents a noun as a comparison standard or describes something as having a similar appearance or quality. Its connective form のようで links the comparison to what follows.

formation.explanation_en: Attach のようだ to a noun to make a comparison or describe resemblance.
Use the connective form to continue the comparison into following material.

entries.title: だ
entries.summary_en: The plain nonpast copula used to identify or describe something.
entries.explanation_en: だ makes a plain assertion after nouns and な-adjective stems. It is the informal counterpart of the polite copula です.

formation.explanation_en: Place だ after a noun or な-adjective stem to make a plain nonpast assertion.

entries.title: い形容詞のく形
entries.reading: いけいようしのくけい
entries.summary_en: Turns an i-adjective into an adverbial modifier or connective form.
entries.explanation_en: The く-form can modify a verb, describing how an action happens, or connect the adjective to a following predicate. The following material determines its role.

formation.form: Replace final い with く
formation.explanation_en: For example, 速い becomes 速く.

entries.title: な形容詞 + になる
entries.reading: なけいようし + になる
entries.summary_en: Describes a change into the state expressed by a な-adjective.
entries.explanation_en: なる means ‘become’ or ‘come to be’. With a な-adjective, に links the adjective to なる and marks the resulting state.

formation.form: な-adjective stem + に + なる
formation.explanation_en: Use に between the adjective stem and なる to express becoming that state.

entries.title: 動詞の辞書形（ plain nonpast）
entries.summary_en: The plain nonpast verb form used for statements and as a base for many constructions.
entries.explanation_en: A verb’s dictionary form is its plain nonpast form. It can describe present habits or general facts, refer to future actions when context supports that reading, and precede constructions that require a plain verb form.

formation.form: Godan verb: retain the final u-row kana
formation.explanation_en: The dictionary form is the verb’s base form, such as 聞く.
The dictionary form ends in る, as in 食べる.
These verbs have the dictionary forms する and 来る（くる）.

entries.title: から (source or origin)
entries.summary_en: Marks a source, starting point, or place from which something emerges.
entries.explanation_en: から follows a place, person, or other source and identifies where movement, transfer, or emergence begins. With a physical opening, it can mark the point from which something comes out.

formation.form: Source + から + movement or emergence predicate
formation.explanation_en: Attach から to the point of origin or source.

entries.title: すると (sequence or consequence)
entries.summary_en: Introduces what happens next or what follows from an event.
entries.explanation_en: すると links a preceding event or situation to a subsequent discovery, result, or development. It commonly presents the next event as occurring in response to or after what came before.

formation.form: Preceding event or situation + すると + following event
formation.explanation_en: Use すると to introduce the next event or consequence.

entries.title: まで
entries.summary_en: Marks an endpoint or extent, meaning “up to” or “until.”
entries.explanation_en: まで marks the limit that a place, time, amount, or range reaches. It can follow a noun or a phrase, including a clause that names an endpoint. With は, the endpoint can be emphasized or contrasted.

formation.explanation_en: Place まで after the phrase that names the endpoint or extent.

entries.title: ので
entries.summary_en: Connects a reason or cause to its result.
entries.explanation_en: ので presents the preceding situation as a reason for what follows. It often sounds measured or explanatory. Attach it to a plain-form clause; a noun or な-adjective normally takes な before ので.

formation.form: Verb or い-adjective plain form + ので
formation.explanation_en: Attach ので directly to the plain form.

formation.form: Noun or な-adjective + な + ので
formation.explanation_en: Use な before ので after a noun or な-adjective.

entries.title: Vてみる
entries.summary_en: Expresses trying an action to see what happens or how it goes.
entries.explanation_en: Attach みる to a verb's て-form to describe carrying out the action as a trial or experiment. The action is presented as something attempted, rather than simply as an intended action.

formation.explanation_en: Use the verb's て-form before みる; the て-form is covered by ja-grammar-te-form.
The resulting construction means to try doing the verb's action.

entries.title: い-adjectiveくなる
entries.reading: いけいようし + くなる
entries.summary_en: Describes a change into the state expressed by an い-adjective.
entries.explanation_en: Replace the final い of an い-adjective with く and add なる. The construction describes becoming or growing into that quality. Its tense and polarity come from なる.

formation.explanation_en: The く form of an い-adjective is covered by ja-grammar-i-adjective-adverbial.
Add なる to describe a change into the adjective's state.

entries.title: 大きな (attributive form)
entries.summary_en: 大きな is a prenominal form meaning “large” or “big.”
entries.explanation_en: 大きな directly modifies a following noun. It is a special attributive form associated with 大きい; it does not follow the regular pattern of い-adjectives, which modify nouns with their い form.

formation.explanation_en: Use 大きな immediately before the noun it describes.

entries.title: い形容詞の非過去形 (述語)
entries.reading: いけいようしのひかこけい（じゅつご）
entries.summary_en: Uses an い-adjective as a plain nonpast predicate.
entries.explanation_en: An い-adjective can end a plain clause and describe its subject or topic. The dictionary form serves as the nonpast predicate; its final い also changes in other adjective forms.

formation.explanation_en: Use the adjective as-is to make a plain nonpast description.

entries.title: に (time point)
entries.summary_en: Marks a specific time when an event occurs.
entries.explanation_en: に follows a time expression that identifies a point at which an event takes place. It is commonly used with specific clock times, dates, and other definite time points; it is often omitted with relative time expressions such as 今日 or 明日.

formation.explanation_en: Place に after the time point associated with the event.

entries.title: に (passive agent)
entries.summary_en: Marks the person or other agent that performs an action in a passive clause.
entries.explanation_en: In a passive clause, に can mark the agent responsible for the action. The affected participant is presented as the subject, while the agent is marked with に.

formation.explanation_en: Place に after the agent in a passive clause; passive verb formation is covered by ja-grammar-passive.

entries.title: を (path or area traversed)
entries.summary_en: Marks a route or area through which movement takes place.
entries.explanation_en: を can mark a place or route that a moving subject passes through, travels along, or leaves. This use is distinct from を marking the direct object of a transitive verb.

formation.form: Place or route + を + verb of movement
formation.explanation_en: Place を after the area traversed or left.

entries.title: では (discourse transition)
entries.summary_en: Introduces a next step or response, often meaning “well then.”
entries.explanation_en: では can mark a transition from what has just been said to a next action, decision, or topic. In this use it functions as a discourse connector, rather than as the copula である.

formation.explanation_en: Used at the start of a clause or utterance to signal a transition.

entries.title: に (location of existence)
entries.summary_en: Marks where a person or thing exists or is present.
entries.explanation_en: に marks the location occupied by a person or thing with an existence predicate such as いる or ある. It identifies where something is, unlike で, which commonly marks where an action takes place.

formation.explanation_en: Put に after the location and use an existence predicate.

entries.title: で (cause or means)
entries.summary_en: Marks a cause, instrument, or means by which an event occurs.
entries.explanation_en: で can identify a cause or means associated with an event, including a natural force that brings about a change. This use differs from で marking the place where an action occurs.

formation.explanation_en: Place で after the cause or means linked to the event.

entries.title: な形容詞 + で (connective form)
entries.summary_en: Connects a な-adjective description to following material.
entries.explanation_en: A な-adjective takes で to link its description to another description, clause, or predicate. The connective form can coordinate descriptions or provide a background state. It is distinct from the location or cause particle で.

formation.explanation_en: Add で directly to the adjective stem, as in 静かで.

entries.title: や (nonexhaustive listing)
entries.summary_en: Lists examples while implying that the list is not complete.
entries.explanation_en: や joins nouns or noun phrases as examples from a broader set. Unlike と in a complete list, や commonly leaves other relevant items unstated.

formation.explanation_en: Use や after an example; additional examples may follow, and the list remains open.

entries.title: Vてから
entries.summary_en: Places one event after completion of the preceding action.
entries.explanation_en: Vてから connects two events and specifies that the second takes place after the first action is completed. It makes the order explicit, while a bare て-form can connect actions without emphasizing that temporal relation.

formation.explanation_en: Attach から to the verb's て-form, then state the later event.
Use the verb's connective form before から.

entries.title: と (companion)
entries.summary_en: Marks a person or group accompanying the subject in an action.
entries.explanation_en: と marks a companion who participates with the subject in an action such as meeting or speaking. In this use it means “with”; it does not mark a quotation or a condition.

formation.explanation_en: Attach と to the person or group accompanying the subject.

entries.title: Vるようになる
entries.summary_en: Describes a change in ability, habit, or state.
entries.explanation_en: ようになる presents an action, ability, or state as something that comes to be true over time. A verb in plain form precedes ように; なる supplies the change-of-state meaning. The tense and polarity are expressed on なる.

formation.form: Verb plain form + ように + なる
formation.explanation_en: Place ようになる after a plain-form verb to describe a change in what happens or is possible.

entries.title: Vて行く (direction away or onward)
entries.summary_en: Combines an action with movement away from the speaker or onward from a reference point.
entries.explanation_en: 行く after a verb's て-form can indicate that the action accompanies movement away from the speaker or another reference point. With a carried object, the construction can mean taking it somewhere. In other contexts, it can present a change or process as continuing onward.

formation.explanation_en: Use the て-form before 行く to connect the action with movement or progression away or onward.

entries.title: のだ
entries.summary_en: Presents a statement as explanatory, clarifying, or emphasized information.
entries.explanation_en: のだ frames a preceding statement as an explanation, clarification, or circumstance being asserted. It follows a plain-form clause; nouns and な-adjectives take な before の. Its tone and force depend on context.

formation.explanation_en: Add のだ after a plain-form clause to give it explanatory or clarifying force.

entries.title: という (reportative)
entries.summary_en: Reports a preceding statement or proposition as something said or reported.
entries.explanation_en: という can follow quoted words or a proposition and present them as reported information. The source may be left unstated; context indicates whether the information is being reported or attributed to someone.

formation.form: Quoted words or plain-form clause + という
formation.explanation_en: Place という after the reported content.

entries.title: 動詞 + まい
entries.summary_en: Expresses a firm intention not to act or a prediction that something will not happen.
entries.explanation_en: まい attaches to a verb to express negative volition or conjecture. With a first-person subject it often conveys a resolve not to do something; with other subjects it can express that an event is unlikely. The form is literary or formal compared with ない or ないだろう.

formation.explanation_en: Attach まい to a verb's dictionary form; する may also appear as すまい.

entries.title: より (comparison)
entries.summary_en: Marks the reference point in a comparison, often meaning “than” or “rather than.”
entries.explanation_en: より follows the item or action used as the basis of comparison. When comparing choices or actions, it can identify what another option is preferred over. The compared item may be a noun or a clause.

formation.explanation_en: Place より after the item or action that serves as the comparison point.

entries.title: Vます-stem + 出す
entries.summary_en: Expresses the beginning or sudden onset of an action or change.
entries.explanation_en: 出す combines with a verb's ます-stem to indicate that the action begins, often suddenly or noticeably. The first verb supplies the action; 出す contributes the onset meaning.

formation.explanation_en: Attach 出す to the verb's ます-stem to form a compound verb.

entries.title: の (subject in an attributive clause)
entries.summary_en: Marks the subject of a clause that modifies a following noun.
entries.explanation_en: In a noun-modifying clause, の can mark the subject of the predicate, much like が does in a standalone clause. This use appears before the predicate inside the modifier; it does not link two nouns to show possession or category.

formation.explanation_en: Place の after the subject within a clause that describes the following noun.

entries.title: 動詞 plain form + 方がよい
entries.reading: どうし plain form + ほうがよい
entries.summary_en: Presents an action or state as the preferable option.
entries.explanation_en: 方がよい treats the preceding verb phrase as one option and says it is better or preferable. The verb phrase can describe an action or a state; context supplies what it is being compared with.

formation.explanation_en: Attach 方がよい to a plain-form verb phrase. The verb phrase identifies the action or state being recommended or preferred.

entries.title: の (within a group)
entries.summary_en: Links a group to a place or selection within it.
entries.explanation_en: After a group or category noun, の can mark that the following 中 is understood relative to that group. 中でも emphasizes a selection as notable even within the group.

formation.explanation_en: 中 refers to the group's interior or membership; でも can add emphasis.

entries.title: N + という (naming)
entries.summary_en: Names or designates someone or something as the preceding noun.
entries.explanation_en: Attach という to a noun to identify something by that name or designation. The connective form といい can continue the naming statement. This naming use differs from sentence-final という that reports a proposition.

formation.explanation_en: The noun supplies the name or designation being assigned.

entries.title: N + というもの
entries.reading: めいし + というもの
entries.summary_en: Frames a noun as a named kind or concept, often for general characterization.
entries.explanation_en: Following a noun, というもの presents it as a kind of thing or as a concept considered broadly. Context determines whether the phrase simply identifies a kind or emphasizes what that kind is like.

formation.explanation_en: Add というもの after a noun to frame it as a named kind or concept.

entries.title: 擬態語 + と (副詞化)
entries.summary_en: Uses と after a mimetic expression to describe how an event occurs.
entries.explanation_en: Many mimetic expressions take と to modify a verb, describing its manner, sound, or quality. The phrase gives the action a vivid manner description.

formation.explanation_en: と connects the mimetic expression adverbially to the event.

entries.title: だの過去形（だった）
entries.summary_en: Forms the plain past of the copula だ.
entries.explanation_en: Use だった to identify or describe something as having been so in the past. Its polite past counterpart is でした.

formation.explanation_en: Replace plain nonpast だ with its plain past form.

entries.title: らしい (推量・伝聞)
entries.summary_en: Presents information as an inference or report rather than direct certainty.
entries.explanation_en: らしい follows a plain-form predicate or noun to present a conclusion or report as indirect information. It can mean “apparently” or “seems.” This evidential use differs from らしい meaning “typical of.”

formation.explanation_en: Attach らしい to a plain-form clause.
After a noun, らしい marks an inference or report about it.

entries.title: 動詞のない形の過去（なかった）
entries.reading: どうしのないけいのかこ
entries.summary_en: Forms the plain past negative of a verb.
entries.explanation_en: Replace the final い of a verb's plain negative ない with かった to say that an action did not happen or was not done.

formation.form: Verb negative in ない + かった
formation.explanation_en: For example, 読まない becomes 読まなかった.

entries.title: はずだ
entries.summary_en: Expresses an expectation or conclusion based on what is known or assumed.
entries.explanation_en: Attach はずだ to a clause to present its proposition as expected or logically likely. Use the plain form with verbs and い-adjectives; use のはずだ after nouns and な-adjectives. Before a noun, はずだ becomes はずの, modifying that noun with the same expectation.

formation.form: Verb or い-adjective plain form + はずだ; noun or な-adjective + のはずだ
formation.explanation_en: Use the plain clause form, adding の after a noun or な-adjective.

formation.form: はずだ → はずの + noun
formation.explanation_en: Use はずの before a noun to make the expected proposition modify it.

entries.title: に (target of encounter)
entries.summary_en: Marks the person or thing encountered with verbs such as 会う.
entries.explanation_en: With 会う, に marks the person or thing one meets. This target marking differs from に for destinations, locations, and passive agents.

formation.form: Person or thing + に + 会う
formation.explanation_en: Place に after the target of the encounter.

entries.title: な形容詞の連体形（な）
entries.reading: なけいようしのれんたいけい
entries.summary_en: Uses な after a な-adjective to modify a following noun.
entries.explanation_en: A な-adjective modifies a noun by placing な between its stem and the noun. This attributive な is part of the adjective’s noun-modifying form.

formation.explanation_en: Add な directly after the adjective stem before the noun.

entries.title: な形容詞の副詞形（に）
entries.reading: なけいようしのふくしけい
entries.summary_en: Uses a な-adjective stem to modify a verb or describe how something occurs.
entries.explanation_en: Attach に to a な-adjective stem to form an adverbial modifier. This grammatical ending differs from the particle に marking a time, location, or target.

formation.explanation_en: Replace attributive な or predicative だ with に.

entries.title: と (comparison reference)
entries.summary_en: Marks the reference point against which something is compared.
entries.explanation_en: と marks the standard of comparison with expressions such as 違う, indicating what something differs from. This use is distinct from と marking a companion or quoted content.

formation.explanation_en: Place と after the reference point being compared.

entries.title: い形容詞の過去形
entries.reading: いけいようしのかこけい
entries.summary_en: Forms the plain past of an i-adjective.
entries.explanation_en: The past form says that a quality held or applied in the past. It can predicate a sentence or modify a noun. It is distinct from the past of a verb or copula.

formation.explanation_en: Remove the final い and add かった, as in 明るい → 明るかった. いい has the irregular past よかった.

entries.title: 動詞のば条件形
entries.reading: どうしのばじょうけんけい
entries.summary_en: Forms a conditional clause meaning “if” or “when.”
entries.explanation_en: The ば-form presents the preceding action or state as a condition for what follows. It can describe a hypothetical condition or a general relationship between condition and result.

formation.form: Godan verb: final う-row kana → corresponding え-row kana + ば
formation.explanation_en: For example, 鳴く → 鳴けば.

formation.form: Ichidan verb: remove る + れば
formation.explanation_en: For example, 食べる → 食べれば.

formation.form: する → すれば; 来る → 来れば
formation.explanation_en: These verbs have irregular ば-forms.

entries.title: に (endured experience or condition)
entries.summary_en: Marks an experience, condition, or burden that someone endures.
entries.explanation_en: With verbs such as 耐える, に marks what is endured or withstood. This use identifies the target of endurance, rather than a location or destination.

formation.explanation_en: The noun names the experience or condition withstood, as in 痛みに耐える, “endure pain.”

entries.title: Vかと思う
entries.summary_en: Expresses a tentative thought or wondering whether something will happen.
entries.explanation_en: A question-shaped clause ending in か can be followed by と and 思う to present its content as a thought or uncertainty. The expression often conveys an expectation that an event might occur. 思う can take its ます-stem 思い to connect the thought to following material.

formation.form: Plain clause + か + と + 思う
formation.explanation_en: Attach か to the clause being considered, then mark it with と before 思う.

entries.title: N + らしい (resemblance or characteristic quality)
entries.summary_en: Describes something as seeming like, or having the qualities associated with, a noun.
entries.explanation_en: After a noun, らしい expresses resemblance or characteristic quality. It can also form a predicate meaning that something seems to be of that type. This use differs from らしい as an evidential that reports or infers information.

formation.explanation_en: Attach らしい directly to a noun; before another noun, it modifies that noun directly.

entries.title: いつの間にか
entries.summary_en: An adverb meaning “before one knows it” or “without noticing when.”
entries.explanation_en: いつの間にか presents an event or change as having occurred without the time or process being noticed. It functions as an adverb in a clause.

formation.explanation_en: This is a set adverbial expression; use it to modify an event or state.

entries.title: な形容詞・名詞 + そうだ (appearance)
entries.reading: なけいようし・めいし + そうだ
entries.summary_en: Describes an appearance or impression based on what is observable.
entries.explanation_en: After a な-adjective stem or noun, そうだ presents something as appearing or seeming to have that quality or identity. With a な-adjective, attach そう directly to its stem; with a noun, use そうだ. This appearance pattern differs from そうだ used to report information.

formation.explanation_en: Attach そうだ to the adjective stem, as in 元気そうだ.
Attach そうだ to a noun to describe an apparent identity or condition.

entries.title: N + と (designation with 決める)
entries.summary_en: Marks the name, role, or status assigned to something with verbs such as 決める.
entries.explanation_en: と marks a noun as the designation or status chosen for someone or something. With 決める, it identifies what the object is decided or designated to be. This use is distinct from と marking a quotation or companion.

formation.form: Object + を + designation + と + 決める
formation.explanation_en: Place と after the noun naming the chosen designation.

entries.title: めったに + negative predicate
entries.reading: めったに + ひていじゅつご
entries.summary_en: Says that something happens rarely or hardly ever, with a negative predicate.
entries.explanation_en: めったに combines with a negative predicate to describe an event as rare or hardly ever occurring. The negative predicate is an essential part of this pattern; めったに does not ordinarily express rarity by itself.

formation.explanation_en: Place めったに before a negative verb or other negative predicate.

entries.title: N + 以外
entries.summary_en: Excludes the named item or group, meaning “except” or “other than.”
entries.explanation_en: 以外 follows a noun phrase and excludes its referent from the range under discussion. The phrase after 以外 can be further modified or marked by particles.

formation.explanation_en: Place 以外 after the item or group to be excluded.

entries.title: 動詞のず形
entries.summary_en: Forms a negative connective meaning “without doing” or “not doing, and…”.
entries.explanation_en: The ず-form gives a verb a negative connective form, linking the negated action to following material. It is common in written and set expressions. する has the irregular form せず; 来る has こず.

formation.form: Ichidan verb: remove final る + ず
formation.explanation_en: For example, 食べる becomes 食べず.

formation.form: Godan verb: change final u-row kana to the corresponding a-row kana + ず
formation.explanation_en: For example, 読む becomes 読まず; verbs ending in う use わ before ず.

formation.form: する → せず; 来る → こず
formation.explanation_en: Use these irregular negative connective forms.

entries.title: に (destination or landing point)
entries.summary_en: Marks the destination or point reached by movement.
entries.explanation_en: に identifies the destination or landing point associated with a movement verb. It focuses on where the subject arrives or gets onto something; へ can instead emphasize direction toward a destination.

formation.form: Destination or landing point + に + movement verb
formation.explanation_en: Place に after the destination or point reached.

entries.title: に (evaluation target)
entries.summary_en: Marks the person or group in relation to whom an evaluation or response applies.
entries.explanation_en: に can mark the person or group toward whom a quality, evaluation, or reaction is directed. The predicate determines the nature of the relationship; this に does not itself mean “destination.”

formation.form: Person or group + に + evaluative predicate
formation.explanation_en: Place に after the person or group that serves as the target of the evaluation.

entries.title: さえ
entries.summary_en: Emphasizes an item as an extreme or unexpected example, meaning “even.”
entries.explanation_en: さえ highlights an item as an especially noteworthy or minimal case. It can occur in positive clauses and, with a negative predicate, emphasize that even the highlighted possibility does not occur.

formation.explanation_en: Place さえ after the item being emphasized.

entries.title: Vた + り + する
entries.summary_en: Lists representative actions or events without presenting them as exhaustive.
entries.explanation_en: The たり pattern presents actions or events as examples from a broader or unspecified set. A verb takes the た-form before り; する can follow the final item to complete the listing predicate. Other forms of する carry the tense and polarity of the construction.

formation.explanation_en: Add り to the verb's た-form to present it as one example.

formation.form: Verb た-form + り + する
formation.explanation_en: Add する after the listed item to form a predicate; further たり phrases can list additional examples.

entries.title: Vてくれる
entries.summary_en: Expresses that someone performs an action for the speaker or someone in the speaker's in-group.
entries.explanation_en: くれる follows a verb's て-form to present the action as a benefit received by the speaker or someone in the speaker's in-group. The main verb supplies the action, while くれる marks the benefactive viewpoint. Tense and polarity are expressed on くれる.

formation.explanation_en: Attach くれる to the verb's て-form; the て-form is covered by ja-grammar-te-form.

entries.title: Vます-stem + かける (incomplete action)
entries.summary_en: Describes an action that has been started but remains unfinished.
entries.explanation_en: かける combines with a verb's ます-stem to describe beginning an action without completing it. The resulting form can modify a noun or function as a predicate; the surrounding form determines how it fits into the sentence.

formation.explanation_en: Attach かける to the ます-stem to form a compound verb.

formation.form: Verb ます-stem + かけ + noun
formation.explanation_en: The ます-stem of the compound can directly modify a noun, as in 読みかけの本.

entries.title: N と N (並列)
entries.reading: めいし と めいし
entries.summary_en: Connects nouns as members of a list, meaning “and.”
entries.explanation_en: と joins nouns into a complete list of the items being named. Unlike や, it does not signal that the list is merely a selection of examples.

formation.explanation_en: Place と between the nouns being connected; additional nouns can be joined with further instances of と.

entries.title: など (例示)
entries.summary_en: Presents an item or list as an example of a broader set.
entries.explanation_en: など indicates that the preceding item or list is illustrative rather than exhaustive. With は, the example can be singled out as a topic or emphasized case.

formation.explanation_en: Follow a noun or list with など to mark it as an example.

entries.title: ほど (おおよその数量)
entries.summary_en: Indicates an approximate amount, extent, or duration.
entries.explanation_en: ほど after a quantity gives an approximate measure, similar to “about” or “approximately.” It can also mark a degree or extent in other constructions.

formation.explanation_en: Place ほど after a number or quantity expression to make the amount approximate.

entries.title: に (行為の対象)
entries.summary_en: Marks the activity, field, or target toward which an action is directed.
entries.explanation_en: に can identify the target or area of an action, including what someone takes up, engages with, or directs their attention toward. The precise relation depends on the predicate; this use differs from marking a destination or location.

formation.explanation_en: Place に after the target or field associated with the predicate.

entries.title: 疑問詞 + でも
entries.summary_en: With an interrogative, でも expresses an unrestricted choice such as “any” or “anything.”
entries.explanation_en: Attached to an interrogative expression, でも removes restrictions on the choice. The resulting phrase can mean “any,” “anyone,” or “anything,” depending on the interrogative. In 何にでも, でも follows the case-marked interrogative phrase.

formation.explanation_en: Attach でも to an interrogative phrase; retain a case particle when the predicate requires one.

entries.title: 名詞 + に (副詞的用法)
entries.summary_en: Uses に after certain nouns to describe the manner or state of an action.
entries.explanation_en: Some nouns, including 一緒, take に to function adverbially and describe how an action is performed or the state in which it occurs. This use is distinct from に marking a destination or time.

formation.explanation_en: Add に to a noun that can describe manner or state, then place it before the verb it modifies.

entries.title: Vてくる (話し手・基準点への移動)
entries.summary_en: Combines an action with movement toward the speaker or a reference point.
entries.explanation_en: After a verb's て-form, 来る can describe movement that brings the action or its result toward the speaker or another reference point. The direction contrasts with て行く, which describes movement away or onward.

formation.explanation_en: Connect the verb to 来る with its て-form; the directional meaning is contributed by 来る.

entries.title: 動詞の意向形（普通体）
entries.reading: どうしのいこうけい（ふつうたい）
entries.summary_en: Expresses the speaker’s intention or an invitation in plain style.
entries.explanation_en: The plain volitional form can express a speaker's intention, such as “I'll do it,” or invite someone to act together, as in “let's do it.” Its use depends on context; it is not the plain nonpast form.

formation.form: Godan verb: final う-row kana → corresponding お-row kana + う
formation.explanation_en: For example, 話す becomes 話そう.

formation.form: Ichidan verb: remove る + よう
formation.explanation_en: For example, 食べる becomes 食べよう.

formation.form: する → しよう; 来る → 来よう（こよう）
formation.explanation_en: These common verbs have irregular volitional forms.

entries.title: のに (逆接・譲歩)
entries.summary_en: Connects a circumstance with a result that is unexpected in light of it.
entries.explanation_en: のに marks a concessive relation, similar to “although” or “even though.” The following clause presents a result that contrasts with what the preceding circumstance would lead one to expect.

formation.explanation_en: Attach のに to a plain-form clause. Nouns and な-adjectives generally use な before のに.

entries.title: な形容詞・名詞 + で (接続)
entries.reading: なけいようし・めいし + で
entries.summary_en: Connects a noun or な-adjective predicate to following material with the copula’s で form.
entries.explanation_en: The copula's で form links a noun or な-adjective description to another predicate or clause. It can coordinate descriptions or provide a circumstance for what follows; here で is the copula form, not the particle marking a place or means.

formation.explanation_en: Use で after a noun in place of plain nonpast だ when connecting to following material.
Use で after the な-adjective stem to connect the description.

entries.title: 形容詞 + さ
entries.summary_en: Turns an adjective into a noun naming a degree or quality.
entries.explanation_en: Attach さ to an adjective stem to name the quality or degree it describes. For an い-adjective, replace final い with さ; with a な-adjective, attach さ to its stem. The resulting noun can take particles and modify other nouns with の.

formation.explanation_en: Replace final い with さ; for example, 高い becomes 高さ.
Attach さ to the adjective stem; for example, 静か becomes 静かさ.

entries.title: Vます-stem + たい
entries.summary_en: Expresses wanting to perform a verb's action.
entries.explanation_en: Attach たい to a verb's ます-stem. The resulting form inflects like an い-adjective, so it can be used with adjective endings such as く. Its subject is usually the person who has the desire; を may change to が for the desired object or action.

formation.explanation_en: Use the same stem that precedes ます, then add たい.

entries.title: Vたい + なる
entries.reading: ぶい + たい + なる
entries.summary_en: Describes a change into wanting to perform an action.
entries.explanation_en: Use the く-form of a Vたい expression before なる to describe desire arising or changing. The form of なる reflects the tense and connection required by the sentence. This construction describes a change in desire; Vたい alone states a desire.

formation.form: Vたい → Vたく + なる
formation.explanation_en: Change the final い of Vたい to く and add なる.
The く-form is the adverbial/connective form of the い-adjective-like desiderative.

entries.title: 動詞の可能形（普通体）
entries.reading: どうしのかのうけい（ふつうたい）
entries.summary_en: Expresses ability or possibility to perform an action.
entries.explanation_en: For godan verbs, change the final u-row kana to its e-row counterpart and add る. For ichidan verbs, replace る with られる; colloquial speech often omits ら. する becomes できる and 来る becomes 来られる. The potential verb conjugates as an ichidan verb.

formation.form: Godan verb: u-row kana → e-row kana + る
formation.explanation_en: For example, 待つ becomes 待てる.

formation.form: Ichidan verb: remove る + られる
formation.explanation_en: For example, 食べる becomes 食べられる.

formation.form: する → できる; 来る → 来られる
formation.explanation_en: These common irregular potential forms must be learned separately.

entries.title: V意向形 + とする
entries.reading: ぶいこうけい + とする
entries.summary_en: Describes trying or being about to perform an action.
entries.explanation_en: Follow a verb's volitional form with とする to present an attempt or an action someone is about to undertake. In the conditional とすると, the phrase can describe what happens when someone tries or is about to act. The volitional form supplies the intended action; とする frames it as an attempt or imminent action.

formation.explanation_en: Place とする after the verb's volitional form.
Use the conditional form of する to frame the attempt or imminent action as a condition.

entries.title: あとで
entries.summary_en: Places an event after a preceding event or time.
entries.explanation_en: あとで follows a noun or an event nominalized with の to locate a later event after it. It can refer to a later time or to what happens once an earlier action is complete.

formation.explanation_en: Use の to connect an event noun to あとで.
Use the plain past form to show that the action is completed before the later event.

entries.title: い形容詞 + そうだ（様態）
entries.reading: いけいようし + そうだ（ようたい）
entries.summary_en: Describes an appearance or impression based on observable signs.
entries.explanation_en: Remove the final い of an い-adjective and add そうだ to describe something as looking or seeming to have that quality. よい becomes よさそうだ. This appearance use differs from hearsay そうだ, which reports information.

formation.explanation_en: Remove final い and add そうだ; よい becomes よさそうだ.

entries.title: そうだ（様態）の副詞形（に）
entries.reading: そうだ（ようたい）のふくしけい（に）
entries.summary_en: Makes an appearance expression modify an action or description.
entries.explanation_en: Replace the final だ of an appearance expression with に when it modifies a verb or describes how an action appears to occur. This に form is adverbial and does not mark a location or target.

formation.form: そうだ（様態） → そうに
formation.explanation_en: Replace the final だ with に.

formation.form: い-adjective stem + そうだ → い-adjective stem + そうに
formation.explanation_en: First form the appearance expression, then use its adverbial に form.

entries.title: に (recipient)
entries.summary_en: Marks the recipient of an action such as giving or providing.
entries.explanation_en: に marks the person or group that receives something in a transfer. With verbs such as 与える, it identifies who is given the object; the thing transferred is commonly marked with を.

formation.form: Recipient + に + object + を + transfer verb
formation.explanation_en: Place に after the recipient and を after the thing transferred.

entries.title: Vたことがある (past experience)
entries.summary_en: States that an action or event has occurred at least once as an experience.
entries.explanation_en: A verb in the た-form followed by ことがある presents the event as something experienced at least once. It commonly describes past experience rather than a particular event in progress; context determines whether the experience is being emphasized.

formation.explanation_en: Use the verb's plain past form.
Turn the past event into a noun phrase with こと.

formation.form: Verb た-form + ことがある
formation.explanation_en: Add がある to state that the event has occurred as an experience.

entries.title: Vたことはない (no past experience)
entries.summary_en: States that an action or event has never occurred as an experience.
entries.explanation_en: A verb in the た-form followed by ことはない denies that the event has ever been experienced. は gives the denial contrastive emphasis. This pattern concerns the absence of an occurrence over the relevant experience period, rather than simply negating a current action.

formation.explanation_en: Use the verb's plain past form.
Turn the past event into a noun phrase with こと.

formation.form: Verb た-form + ことはない
formation.explanation_en: Use はない to deny that the nominalized event has occurred.

entries.title: Vるうち (while; over the course of)
entries.summary_en: Places a development within the time or process of an action or state.
entries.explanation_en: うち follows a plain nonpast verb to frame what follows as happening while an action or state continues, or as developing over its course. With repeated or ongoing activity, it can describe a change that emerges gradually during that period.

formation.explanation_en: Place うち after a plain nonpast verb to set the period or process within which the following event or development occurs.

entries.title: も (emphatic “even”)
entries.summary_en: Adds emphatic focus, often meaning “even.”
entries.explanation_en: も focuses the phrase before it as an included or unexpected case. With a quoted thought or judgment, it can emphasize that the thought did not occur, as in 怖いとも思わない, “not even think it is scary.” Its contribution depends on the phrase it follows and the wider sentence.

formation.explanation_en: Place も after the phrase to add it to the set under consideration or mark it as an emphatic case.

entries.title: Vます-stem + 始める
entries.reading: ますごかん + はじめる
entries.summary_en: Expresses the beginning of an action.
entries.explanation_en: Attach 始める to a verb’s ます-stem to say that the action begins. 始める then inflects as a verb; the lexical action remains in the first verb.

formation.explanation_en: Use the verb’s ます-stem before 始める; for example, 動き始める means “begin to move.”

entries.title: N、N (approximate range)
entries.summary_en: Joins nearby quantities to give an approximate range.
entries.explanation_en: Two quantities joined by a comma can indicate a range between them, often “two or three” or “a few.” A counter may follow the second quantity and apply to the range.

formation.explanation_en: Place the two quantities around a Japanese comma; attach the relevant counter to the second quantity, as in 二、三ページ, “two or three pages.”

entries.title: Vずにいる
entries.summary_en: Describes remaining in a state without performing an action.
entries.explanation_en: The negative connective ずに precedes いる to describe continuing or remaining without doing the action. The tense and politeness of いる determine the form of the whole predicate.

formation.form: Verb ない-stem + ずに + いる
formation.explanation_en: Use the verb’s negative ず-form followed by に and いる; する has the irregular form せずにいる.

entries.title: 普通形 + ようだ
entries.reading: ふつうけい + ようだ
entries.summary_en: Describes something as seeming or resembling what a preceding clause expresses.
entries.explanation_en: Attach ようだ to a plain-form clause to present an impression, inference, or resemblance. The attributive form ような modifies a noun. A noun instead commonly takes のようだ; this clause pattern does not use の.

formation.explanation_en: Attach ようだ directly to a plain-form verb or adjective clause to express that something seems to be or is like that state or event.
Use ような before a noun to describe it as seeming or resembling the preceding clause.

entries.title: 節 + の (名詞化)
entries.summary_en: Turns a clause into a noun-like phrase that can fill a sentence role.
entries.explanation_en: Attach の to a clause to refer to its event, fact, or content as a noun-like phrase. The resulting phrase can be marked by particles such as は or が. This clause-nominalizing の is distinct from の linking two nouns.

formation.explanation_en: Place の after a clause to make its event, fact, or content function as a noun-like phrase.

entries.title: N + にとって
entries.summary_en: Marks the person or group from whose viewpoint something is considered.
entries.explanation_en: にとって sets a viewpoint or standard of relevance, often translated as “for” or “from the perspective of.” It usually follows a noun referring to a person or group.

formation.explanation_en: Attach にとって to a noun naming the person or group whose viewpoint is relevant.

entries.title: 普通形 + のだろう
entries.reading: ふつうけい + のだろう
entries.summary_en: Presents an explanation or conclusion as a conjecture.
entries.explanation_en: のだろう frames a proposition as an explanatory inference or supposition. It combines the explanatory のだ pattern with だろう, which signals uncertainty; it is not simply a statement of fact.

formation.explanation_en: Attach のだろう to a plain-form clause. With a noun or な-adjective, use なのだろう.

entries.title: ではない
entries.summary_en: Forms the plain negative of a noun or な-adjective predicate.
entries.explanation_en: ではない negates a noun or な-adjective predicate in plain style. は adds contrastive emphasis to the copula’s で connection; じゃない is a common contracted form. With だけ, ではない can negate the claim that something is the only item or extent.

formation.form: N / な-adjective stem + ではない
formation.explanation_en: Use ではない after a noun or な-adjective stem to say that it is not that thing or state.

entries.title: も (addition)
entries.summary_en: Adds an item to an existing set or statement, often meaning “also” or “too.”
entries.explanation_en: も marks an item as included alongside another item or an understood set. It commonly takes the place of a particle such as が or を; with に, it follows に to add the marked recipient, target, or location.

formation.explanation_en: Place も after the phrase being added. When another particle is needed, it may follow that particle, as in Nにも.

entries.title: V plain form + まま
entries.reading: どうしのふつうけい + まま
entries.summary_en: Describes something continuing while a state remains unchanged.
entries.explanation_en: まま presents a state as continuing without change while another event or situation holds. It can follow a verb in forms such as Vたまま or Vないまま, and a noun with の. The preceding form identifies the state that remains.

formation.explanation_en: Attach まま to a verb form describing the continuing state; Vないまま describes continuing without doing the action.

entries.title: Vて + も (concession)
entries.reading: どうしのてけい + も（ぎゃくせつ）
entries.summary_en: Presents an action or situation as a condition that does not change the outcome.
entries.explanation_en: Vて + も means “even if” or “even when” the action occurs. With a degree word such as いくら, it can mean that no matter how much or how often the action occurs, the result remains the same.

formation.explanation_en: Add も to the verb's て-form to mark the condition as concessive.

entries.title: まで (emphatic addition)
entries.reading: まで（きょうちょうてきなついか）
entries.summary_en: Adds an unexpected or extreme item, meaning “even.”
entries.explanation_en: After a noun or noun phrase, まで can extend a set to an unexpected or extreme case. In this use it emphasizes inclusion, unlike まで marking an endpoint in space, time, or extent.

formation.explanation_en: Place まで after the item emphasized as an additional or extreme case.

entries.title: ほど (degree or extent)
entries.summary_en: Marks a degree or extent, often introducing a result that reaches that degree.
entries.explanation_en: ほど follows a phrase to indicate its degree or extent. In patterns such as “so ... that,” the following clause can describe a result reached at that degree. This use is distinct from ほど after quantities to indicate an approximate amount.

formation.explanation_en: Place ほど after the phrase whose degree or extent is being indicated.

entries.title: 普通形 + かもしれない
entries.reading: ふつうけい + かもしれない
entries.summary_en: Expresses that a possibility is uncertain: “might” or “may.”
entries.explanation_en: Attach かもしれない to a plain-form predicate to present its content as possible but uncertain. With nouns and な-adjectives, だ is generally omitted before かもしれない. It expresses less certainty than a direct assertion and does not itself mark past time; the predicate conveys the time reference.

formation.form: Verb or い-adjective plain form + かもしれない
formation.explanation_en: Follows the plain form of a verb or い-adjective.

formation.form: Noun or な-adjective stem + かもしれない
formation.explanation_en: Follows a noun or な-adjective without だ.

entries.title: い形容詞のば条件形
entries.reading: いけいようしのばじょうけんけい
entries.summary_en: Forms a conditional clause with an い-adjective, meaning “if” or “when.”
entries.explanation_en: Replace the final い of an い-adjective with ければ. The result presents the adjective’s quality as a condition. The negative adjective ない follows the same pattern, becoming なければ.

formation.explanation_en: For example, 高い becomes 高ければ; ない becomes なければ.

entries.title: 動詞辞書形 + なり（即時）
entries.reading: どうしじしょけい + なり
entries.summary_en: Says that an event follows immediately after the preceding verb’s action.
entries.explanation_en: This construction presents the second event as happening as soon as the first action occurs. It has a literary or formal tone and commonly takes a verb in dictionary form before なり.

formation.explanation_en: Attach なり directly to a verb in dictionary form; the following clause gives the immediately subsequent event.

entries.title: Vてくる（変化の出現・進展）
entries.reading: てくる（へんかのしゅつげん・しんてん）
entries.summary_en: Describes an action or change emerging or developing toward a reference point, often the present.
entries.explanation_en: This use of てくる presents an action, state, or change as beginning to appear or developing toward the speaker’s reference point in time. With weather and other changes, it can convey that something has begun or is coming to be. It uses the て-form followed by くる; context distinguishes this developing sense from physical movement toward the speaker.

formation.explanation_en: Combine the verb’s て-form with くる to show emergence or development toward a reference point.

entries.title: Vない + ように (purpose or desired outcome)
entries.summary_en: States an intended outcome or purpose, often with a preceding negative form.
entries.explanation_en: ように links an action to an outcome someone aims for or takes steps to bring about. With a potential, state, or negative clause before it, it often means “so that” or “in order to.” The following clause commonly describes an action taken to achieve that outcome.

formation.explanation_en: Use the plain negative before ように to express an aim such as avoiding an outcome.

formation.form: Vる / potential form + ように
formation.explanation_en: A plain or potential form can precede ように to express an outcome being aimed for.

notes_en: Distinguish purpose ように from ようだ, which expresses resemblance or an impression.

entries.title: Clause + し (listing reasons or circumstances)
entries.summary_en: Adds a reason or circumstance to a non-exhaustive list.
entries.explanation_en: し follows a predicate and presents its clause as one reason, circumstance, or characteristic among others. It can connect multiple clauses or leave the list open, often giving a cumulative explanation.

formation.explanation_en: Attach し to a plain-form verb, adjective, or copula predicate.
Use だ before し after a noun or な-adjective predicate.

notes_en: し is a clause-linking particle here, not the verb ます-stem or the conjunctive stem.

entries.title: V / clause + ことが多い
entries.reading: どうし・せつ + ことがおおい
entries.summary_en: Says that an action or event occurs often.
entries.explanation_en: こと turns an action or clause into an event or fact, and が多い characterizes such events as frequent. The construction describes a recurring tendency rather than a single event.

formation.form: Plain-form verb or clause + ことが多い
formation.explanation_en: Nominalize the action or clause with こと, then say that such events are frequent.

notes_en: The predicate before こと is normally in plain form.

entries.title: V / clause + ことさえある
entries.reading: どうし・せつ + ことさえある
entries.summary_en: Says that an event can occur even as an extreme or unexpected case.
entries.explanation_en: こと nominalizes an action or clause; さえ adds emphatic focus, and ある presents the event as one that occurs. Together they highlight that even this event sometimes happens.

formation.form: Plain-form verb or clause + ことさえある
formation.explanation_en: Nominalize the event with こと, then use さえある to emphasize its occurrence as an extreme or unexpected case.

notes_en: Compared with こともある, ことさえある emphasizes the event as an extreme or surprising instance.

entries.title: N + ながら (concession)
entries.summary_en: Concedes a circumstance, meaning “although” or “despite being.”
entries.explanation_en: ながら can follow a noun to present that identity or circumstance as a concession to the main statement. The main clause supplies the point that holds despite the stated circumstance.

formation.explanation_en: Attach ながら directly to a noun to concede the circumstance it names.

notes_en: This concessive noun pattern is distinct from verb ます-stem + ながら, which describes simultaneous actions.

entries.title: 普通形 + なら
entries.summary_en: Takes a stated or assumed situation as the premise for what follows.
entries.explanation_en: なら frames a situation as a condition for a judgment, recommendation, or consequence. It can follow nouns, な-adjectives, and plain-form clauses. With a verb or い-adjective, it often takes up a proposition as a premise; unlike と, it does not present the result as automatic or regular.

formation.explanation_en: Attach なら directly to a noun or な-adjective.

formation.form: Verb / い-adjective plain form + なら
formation.explanation_en: Follow the plain-form proposition with なら.

entries.title: だって (emphatic addition)
entries.summary_en: Adds an item as an emphatic or unexpected example, often meaning “even.”
entries.explanation_en: だって attaches to a noun or noun phrase to include it in a set while emphasizing that it is an unexpected or noteworthy case. In this use it resembles も, often with stronger emphasis. Its other uses, including quotation-like “they say,” depend on context.

formation.explanation_en: Attach directly to the emphasized noun phrase.

entries.title: Vないことはない
entries.summary_en: Says that an action or possibility is not entirely ruled out, often as a qualified affirmation.
entries.explanation_en: A verb's plain negative form followed by ことはない presents the absence of a case in which the action is impossible. The whole pattern means that the action is possible or not impossible, often with some reservation.

formation.form: Verb plain negative + ことはない
formation.explanation_en: Nominalize the negative verb with こと and follow it with はない to express qualified possibility.

entries.title: Vる / N + たびに
entries.reading: る / めいし + たびに
entries.summary_en: Says that something occurs every time the specified event or occasion occurs.
entries.explanation_en: たびに links a recurring event or occasion to what happens on each occurrence. With verbs it follows the dictionary form; with nouns it usually follows の.

formation.explanation_en: Place たびに after a verb in dictionary form.
Use の to connect a noun to たび before に.

entries.title: 動詞の使役形
entries.summary_en: Forms a verb that presents someone as causing or allowing an action.
entries.explanation_en: The causative form indicates that a subject makes or lets another participant perform the verb's action. Whether the situation is coercive or permissive depends on context and the verb. With many transitive verbs, the person made to act is marked by に; with many intransitive verbs, を is common. Ichidan verbs add させる, godan verbs change the final う-row kana to the corresponding あ-row kana and add せる, and する and 来る have the irregular forms させる and 来させる.

formation.explanation_en: For example, 食べる becomes 食べさせる.

formation.form: Godan verb: final う-row kana → あ-row kana + せる
formation.explanation_en: For example, 言う becomes 言わせる; う changes to わ before せる.

formation.form: する → させる; 来る → 来させる
formation.explanation_en: These are the irregular causative forms.

entries.title: 動詞の可能形
entries.summary_en: Expresses ability or possibility to perform an action.
entries.explanation_en: The potential form presents an action as possible or within someone's ability. The person with that ability is often marked by が or は; を may be replaced by が with a potential verb. Ichidan verbs add られる, godan verbs change the final kana to the corresponding え-row kana and add る, and する and 来る have the forms できる and 来られる.

formation.explanation_en: For example, 食べる becomes 食べられる.

formation.form: Godan verb: final う-row kana → え-row kana + る
formation.explanation_en: For example, 書く becomes 書ける.

formation.form: する → できる; 来る → 来られる
formation.explanation_en: These are the potential forms of the irregular verbs.

entries.title: Vて + もらう
entries.summary_en: Presents an action as a favor or service received by the subject.
entries.explanation_en: The subject receives the benefit of another person's action. The person who performs the action is commonly marked by に. The subject's viewpoint determines who counts as receiving the benefit; the construction does not itself say that the action was requested.

formation.explanation_en: Connect the action in its て-form to もらう; conjugate もらう for the desired tense, polarity, or politeness.

entries.title: 節 + ことから
entries.summary_en: Treats a fact or circumstance as the source or basis for a conclusion.
entries.explanation_en: ことから nominalizes the preceding fact and presents it as evidence, a basis, or a cause for what follows. It often makes the inferential link explicit.

formation.explanation_en: Follow a plain-form clause with ことから; a noun or な-adjective predicate can use である before ことから.

entries.title: に (可能の主体)
entries.summary_en: Marks the person or entity for whom an action is possible or within reach.
entries.explanation_en: With potential predicates, に can identify the participant whose ability or possibility is being evaluated. は or も may follow に to mark topic or emphasis. This participant role differs from に marking an action's recipient, destination, or location.

formation.explanation_en: Place に after the person or entity whose ability is at issue.

entries.title: に (viewpoint holder with 言わせる)
entries.summary_en: Marks whose viewpoint is presented in the expression Nに言わせると.
entries.explanation_en: In the expression Nに言わせると, に marks the person whose opinion or account provides the viewpoint. The whole expression means “according to N” or “in N's view.”

formation.form: Person or group + に + 言わせると
formation.explanation_en: Place に after the viewpoint holder in this expression.

entries.title: Nに言わせると
entries.reading: めいし に いわせると
entries.summary_en: Introduces an assessment or account from someone's viewpoint: “according to N.”
entries.explanation_en: Nに言わせると presents what follows as the opinion or account of N. Though 言わせる has causative form, the expression conventionally marks a viewpoint; it does not normally assert that someone was made to speak.

formation.form: Person or group + に + 言わせると
formation.explanation_en: Follow the person whose view is being presented with に言わせると.

entries.title: から (reason or cause)
entries.summary_en: Links a stated reason or cause to a result.
entries.explanation_en: から attaches to a clause that gives the reason or cause for what follows. With a noun or な-adjective predicate, だから is used before から; with a verb or い-adjective, the plain form can be followed directly by から. It often presents the reason directly, while ので can sound more explanatory or less assertive.

formation.explanation_en: Attach から to a plain clause; use だから after a noun or な-adjective predicate.

entries.title: 普通形 + というわけではない
entries.reading: ふつうけい + というわけではない
entries.summary_en: Denies that a preceding statement is the case or the intended explanation.
entries.explanation_en: This pattern follows a plain clause and rejects it as a conclusion, interpretation, or explanation. It often means “it is not that…” or “that does not mean…,” and can soften a denial by addressing the proposed reasoning rather than simply negating a predicate.

formation.form: Plain clause + というわけではない
formation.explanation_en: Place というわけではない after a plain clause; with a noun or な-adjective predicate, use だ before という.

entries.title: ものだ (general characterization)
entries.reading: ものだ（そうごうてきなせいしつ）
entries.summary_en: Characterizes something as having a general or typical quality.
entries.explanation_en: ものだ after a noun phrase or clause presents the described quality as characteristic or general. With a noun or な-adjective, use な before もの; verbs and い-adjectives use their plain form. Its force depends on context and can be descriptive rather than a literal statement about an object.

formation.form: Noun / な-adjective + な + ものだ
formation.explanation_en: Use な to connect a noun or な-adjective to ものだ.

formation.form: Verb / い-adjective plain form + ものだ
formation.explanation_en: Attach ものだ directly to a plain-form clause.

entries.title: Potential negative + なる
entries.reading: かのうひてい + なる
entries.summary_en: Describes becoming unable to do something or a loss of ability.
